newsitem.title: UK: ZENECA SEES FULL-YEAR DRUG MARGINS 30 PCT.
newsitem.headline: ZENECA SEES FULL-YEAR DRUG MARGINS 30 PCT.

text.p: Britain's Zeneca Group Plc said on Thursday it expected full-year profit margins at its core pharmaceuticals business to decline slightly to 30 percent from 31.1 percent in 1996, in line with previous forecasts.

Finance director John Mayo, who is leaving the company to join Britain's General Electric Co Plc in October, told a news conference the continuing strength of sterling, lower currency hedging benefits and new product launch costs would all contribute to the reduction in margin.
He added that at agrochemicals, "Adverse currency effects and increased costs associated with the roll-out of new products are likely to have a dampening effect on profit growth in the second half."

Mayo also said the group's "negligible" gearing of 3.7 percent was likely to rise by the end of the year "given the potential for further minor acquisitions in the second half of the year, such as ICI Australia's pharmaceutical business."
Mayo added that Zeneca was "firing on all cylinders and has produced another fine set of results."

"However, investors should not get carried away by 22 percent underlying profit growth in the first half. The second half will be tougher, with higher new product launch costs. Nevertheless, we expect the underlying performance for the full year to be broadly in line with the group's aspirational target of 15 percent compound earnings growth," he added.
